title: podman build --secret leaves secrets in plaintext next to the build context
body:
### Issue Description

A successful `podman build --secret` leaves a plaintext copy of the secret on the host and does not remove it. The copy lands in the parent directory of the build context, mode 0600. Not in `TMPDIR` or somewhere else.

This looks like a leftover from #28356, which fixed #25314 and #28334 by moving these temp files under the primary context. Both of those were about the secret ending up inside the image, or the build failing. This is the opposite direction: the build succeeds, the image is clean, and the secret stays on the host.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

No compose, no registry, no `.dockerignore`. Build from a third directory:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/fixture/ctx /tmp/fixture/elsewhere
echo "s3cr3t-value" > /tmp/fixture/mysecret
printf 'FROM docker.io/library/alpine:3.20\nRUN --mount=type=secret,id=tok cat /run/secrets/tok\n' \
  > /tmp/fixture/ctx/Dockerfile

cd /tmp/fixture/elsewhere
podman build --secret id=tok,src=/tmp/fixture/mysecret -t leaktest /tmp/fixture/ctx
ls -l /tmp/fixture
```

### Describe the results you received

The build succeeds, with no error and no warning:
```
STEP 2/2: RUN --mount=type=secret,id=tok cat /run/secrets/tok
s3cr3t-value
COMMIT leaktest
--> 5731f2f459f9
Successfully tagged localhost/leaktest:latest
```

The secret is then sitting in the context's parent:
```bash
$ find /tmp/fixture | sort
/tmp/fixture
/tmp/fixture/ctx
/tmp/fixture/ctx/Dockerfile
/tmp/fixture/elsewhere
/tmp/fixture/mysecret
/tmp/fixture/podman-build-secret-1695017466      <- left behind

$ ls -l /tmp/fixture/podman-build-secret-1695017466
-rw-------  1 me  wheel  13 Aug 31 16:17 /tmp/fixture/podman-build-secret-1695017466

$ cat /tmp/fixture/podman-build-secret-1695017466
s3cr3t-value                                      <- the secret, in plaintext
```

Two things about the location:
- Not the working directory. The build ran from `/tmp/fixture/elsewhere`, which stayed empty.
- Not the context. `/tmp/fixture/ctx` still holds only the Dockerfile.

The second one surprised me, because the code passes the context directory. In v6.1.0, `prepareSecrets` does:
```go
tmpSecret, err := tempManager.CreateTempFileFromReader(contextDir, "podman-build-secret-*", ...)
```
and `CreateTempFileFromReader` is a plain `os.CreateTemp(dest, pattern)`. So I would expect the file in the context, not one level above it.

### Describe the results you expected

The file is removed when the build finishes. That already looks like the intent: `build()` has `defer tempManager.Cleanup()`, `CreateTempFileFromReader` registers the file with `AddFile` before writing to it, and `Cleanup()` calls `os.Remove` on everything registered.

`Cleanup()` also logs `Failed to remove temp file %s: %v` on any error other than "already gone", and there is no such line in the output. So cleanup is not failing loudly. It is not reaching this file at all.

### podman info output

```yaml
Client:
  APIVersion: 6.1.0
  BuildOrigin: brew
  Built: 1786554266
  BuiltTime: Wed Aug 12 19:04:26 2026
  GoVersion: go1.26.5
  Os: darwin
  OsArch: darwin/arm64
  Version: 6.1.0
host:
  arch: arm64
  buildahVersion: 1.44.0
  cgroupManager: systemd
  cgroupVersion: v2
  cpus: 10
  databaseBackend: sqlite
  distribution:
    distribution: fedora
    variant: podman-machine-os
    version: "44"
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

```bash
$ podman version
Client:  Version: 6.1.0   Build Origin: brew   OS/Arch: darwin/arm64
Server:  Version: 6.1.0   OS/Arch: linux/arm64

$ podman machine ssh rpm -q podman
podman-6.1.0-1.20260812170728687735.pr29481.11.cade97a52e.fc44.aarch64

$ podman machine ssh sudo bootc status | grep image:
    image: quay.io/podman/machine-os:6.1

$ sw_vers
ProductName:     macOS
ProductVersion:  26.6.2
BuildVersion:    25G83

$ system_profiler SPHardwareDataType
Model Name:       MacBook Pro
Model Identifier: Mac16,7
Chip:             Apple M4 Pro
...
```
applehv, rootless. Nothing configured on my side: no `containers.conf` and no `storage.conf` at either `~/.config/containers/` or `/etc/containers/`. The repro has no `.dockerignore` at all, so #25314 seems like a different issue.

### Additional information

Impact, in case it is not obvious from something that looks like a stray temp file: this is a credential written to a directory the user did not choose and is not watching. In my case it was a short-lived Google Artifact Registry token, so a handful accumulated next to my repo checkouts before I noticed, which is survivable. A long-lived secret would not be. A build context at the root of a synced folder would not be either.
